t: An Ismaili Shia caliphate born of a secret missionary network in North Africa, set up in 910 as a rival to Abbasid Baghdad.
From Cairo, which it founded, it controlled Red Sea to Mediterranean trade and built al-Azhar, still a leading centre of Islamic learning.
Famine, army factions and a schism in 1094 eroded it until Saladin quietly restored Abbasid prayers in 1171.
dyk: The Nizari Ismailis who broke away after the 1094 succession crisis gave rise to the imams known today as the Aga Khans, a lineage tracing back to the Fatimid missionary network.
ev: Abdallah al-Mahdi Billah is proclaimed caliph at Raqqada after the Kutama overthrow the Aghlabids
General Jawhar al-Siqilli conquers Egypt; Cairo is founded north of Fustat
The al-Azhar mosque is begun, later developing into a great teaching institution
The Zirid governor of Ifriqiya renounces Fatimid allegiance, severing North Africa
Badr al-Jamali arrives and takes over as vizier and commander after years of chaos
Succession crisis over Nizar splits the Ismaili community permanently
Saladin restores prayers for the Abbasid caliph; the last Fatimid caliph al-Adid dies
